title: Exam Orientation and the Command-Line Toolkit

header.html: exam environment and speed kit (supports every competency)

toc.title: JSONPath and custom columns (a frequent time-saver)
A repeatable way to work every task

html:
1What the exam is

The exam is performance-based. You get a live terminal, not multiple-choice questions. You solve real tasks on a real cluster, and a script scores the final cluster state, not the commands you typed. The CKAD tests what an application developer does every day: build and run Pods, deploy and update them, configure them, secure them, observe them and expose them.

Item Value (official pages, read 2026-11-15)
Format 15 to 20 performance-based tasks in a command line, online proctored
Duration 2 hours
Kubernetes version v1.37
Passing score 66%
Price USD 445, exam only; includes one retake
Validity 2 years
Simulator killer.sh, 2 attempts of 36 hours each; each session has 17 questions
Results Emailed within 24 hours
Prerequisites None; working knowledge of container runtimes and microservice architecture is assumed

Not published on the pages used for this course: how many clusters you will switch between, the exact points per task, and which tool builds images in the exam environment. Do not rely on a number from a blog. Read the context line of every task.

Domain weights

Domain Weight Where it is taught
Application Environment, Configuration and Security 25% Modules 9 to 13
Application Design and Build 20% Modules 1 to 4
Application Deployment 20% Modules 5 and 6
Services and Networking 20% Modules 14 to 16
Application Observability and Maintenance 15% Modules 7 and 8

Exam focus: time goes where points are. Configuration and security is a quarter of the score, and the other four domains share the rest almost evenly. Every module also has a break-and-fix task, because a Pod that does not start is the most common reason for losing a task.

2The exam environment

  • You start on a host called base. Tasks name the host to use, and you reach it with ssh <node>. You cannot SSH from one node to another (no nested SSH). Type exit to return to base. Use sudo -i to become root on a node.
  • Every task begins with a context line, usually a kubectl config use-context ... command. Run it first. Working in the wrong cluster scores zero.
  • kubectl is installed on the task hosts with the alias k and shell autocompletion. Also installed there: yq, curl, wget, man. These tools are not on base itself.
  • The Insert key is prohibited. Do not reboot base. Copy and paste in the terminal with Ctrl+Shift+C and Ctrl+Shift+V.
  • Allowed documentation: kubernetes.io/docs and the Kubernetes blog, helm.sh/docs, the Quick Reference links in the exam, and distribution documents under /usr/share. The kubernetes.io search is allowed. Do not open external search results. (The Gateway API site is allowed for the CKA only, not for the CKAD.)

In this course's lab cluster there is no ssh. A small wrapper turns ssh ckad-worker 'command' into docker exec. Everything else (kubectl, files, manifests) behaves as on the exam. Files you are asked to save go to ~/answers/ on the machine where you run kubectl. The CKAD asks you to work with kubectl almost all of the time, so node access matters far less than in the CKA.

3The speed kit

Typing YAML by hand is slow. Generate it, then edit.

export do="--dry-run=client -o yaml"      # then:  k run web --image=nginx:alpine $do > pod.yaml
export now="--force --grace-period 0"     # then:  k delete pod web $now
alias kn='kubectl config set-context --current --namespace'
Need Command
Pod k run web --image=nginx:alpine --labels=tier=web
Pod with a command k run job1 --image=busybox:1.36 -- sleep 3600
Deployment k create deployment api --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=3
Job and CronJob k create job once --image=busybox:1.36 -- date, k create cronjob tick --image=busybox:1.36 --schedule="*/10 * * * *" -- date
ConfigMap and Secret k create configmap app --from-literal=a=1, k create secret generic db --from-literal=pw=x
Service for something that exists k expose deployment api --port=80
Any object as a template add --dry-run=client -o yaml
Find a field name k explain pod.spec.containers --recursive or k explain pod.spec | grep -i grace
List with more columns k get pods -o wide
One value k get pod web -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}'
Loop over items -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}'
Chosen columns -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,IMG:.spec.containers[0].image
Sort --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
Default namespace k config set-context --current --namespace=speed
Can this account do it? k auth can-i get pods --as system:serviceaccount:dev:app -n dev

Editor: vim is the safe choice. Put set expandtab tabstop=2 shiftwidth=2 in ~/.vimrc so pasted YAML keeps its indentation.

kubectl explain beats searching. It shows the exact field names for the cluster version you are on, with no browser and no tab-switching. Use --recursive for the whole tree.

Read the whole task before typing. The scoring script checks every sentence of the task. A missing label or the wrong namespace costs the full task.

Imperative first, declarative when needed

Imperative commands (run, create, expose, set, scale, label) are fastest for simple objects. When a field has no flag (probes, volumes, security context), generate YAML with --dry-run=client -o yaml, edit it, and apply -f. For a running object, k edit changes it in place, though many Pod fields cannot be changed after creation: then delete and recreate (k replace --force -f pod.yaml).

3b. Labels and selectors (they connect everything)

Labels are key/value tags on objects; Services, Deployments, NetworkPolicies and kubectl filters all find objects by label.

k get pods --show-labels
k get pods -l stage=live                     # equality selector
k get pods -l 'stage in (live,test),tier!=db' # set-based selector
k label pod p1 stage=live --overwrite        # add or change a label (--overwrite to change)
k label pod p1 stage-                        # remove the label (trailing minus)
k delete pods -l stage=test                  # act on every match
k annotate pod p1 note="checked"             # annotations: free-form metadata, not selectable

A Service or Deployment selector that does not match the Pod template labels is a classic exam fault (Modules 5 and 14).

4JSONPath and custom columns (a frequent time-saver)

jsonpath pulls exact values out of an object, which is how tasks such as "write the image of every Pod to a file" are solved:

k -n inv get pods -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.spec.containers[0].image}{"\n"}{end}' | sort > images.txt
  • {.items[*].metadata.name} prints names on one line separated by spaces.
  • range ... end plus {"\n"} puts one per line.
  • -o name prints pod/<name>; if the task wants the bare name, use jsonpath or sed.
  • custom-columns prints a header unless you remove it (--no-headers); check the task for "without header".

5A repeatable way to work every task

  1. Read the task and the context line; run the use-context command.
  2. Note the namespace and the names given. Use them exactly.
  3. Do the task with the fastest command.
  4. Verify with one command (k get, k describe, k logs, curl). A task that "should" work and does not is the most common loss.
  5. If a task is stuck after about 6 minutes, flag it, move on, and return at the end.

With 2 hours and 15 to 20 tasks, you have about 6 to 8 minutes per task on average. The easy tasks (a ConfigMap, a label, a Service) take 2 minutes, which buys time for the multi-step ones.

6Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m00 -->

Lab 0.1: jsonpath pod images

Domain: Observability | Points: 3 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m00-01-jsonpath-pod-images)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace inv, three Pods are running. Write one line per Pod to ~/answers/images.txt on the host where you run kubectl (the exam's base host), in the form <pod name> <image>, sorted by Pod name, with no header line.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n inv get pods -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.spec.containers[0].image}{"\n"}{end}' | sort > ~/answers/images.txt
cat ~/answers/images.txt

Lab 0.2: dry run deployment

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m00-02-dry-run-deployment)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

Create the namespace speed. Generate (do not hand-write) a manifest for a Deployment named shop with image nginx:alpine and 2 replicas, and save it to ~/answers/deploy.yaml. Then create the Deployment from that file in the namespace speed and wait until both replicas are Ready.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl create ns speed
kubectl -n speed create deployment shop --image=nginx:alpine --replicas=2 --dry-run=client -o yaml > ~/answers/deploy.yaml
kubectl apply -f ~/answers/deploy.yaml -n speed
kubectl -n speed rollout status deployment shop --timeout=120s

Lab 0.3: explain field

Domain: Design and Build | Points: 3 | Time: about 3 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m00-03-explain-field)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

Without opening a browser, use kubectl explain to find the name of the Pod spec field that makes a Pod use the network namespace of the node it runs on. Write only the field name, with the exact capitalization, to ~/answers/field.txt.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl explain pod.spec | grep -i hostnetwork
echo hostNetwork > ~/answers/field.txt

Lab 0.4: default namespace

Domain: Environment | Points: 3 | Time: about 3 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m00-04-default-namespace)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

Create the namespace speed. Change the current context so that kubectl uses speed as its default namespace, without editing any file by hand and without changing the context name.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl create ns speed
kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=speed

Lab 0.5: labels selectors

Domain: Observability | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m00-05-labels-selectors)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace lbl, three Pods exist: p1, p2 and p3, each with the label stage=test. Change the label stage of p1 and p2 to live (do not recreate them). Write the names of all Pods with stage=live, one per line and sorted, to ~/answers/live.txt on the host, using a label selector. Then delete all Pods that still have stage=test using a label selector (not by name).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n lbl label pod p1 p2 stage=live --overwrite
kubectl -n lbl get pods --show-labels
kubectl -n lbl get pods -l stage=live -o name | sed 's#pod/##' | sort > ~/answers/live.txt
kubectl -n lbl delete pods -l stage=test

<!-- /LABS -->

7Recall questions

R1What does the exam score: the commands you typed or the final cluster state?

Show the answer

The final cluster state.

R2What is the first action on every task?

Show the answer

Run the context line (the kubectl config use-context command) given in the task.

R3Which domain carries the highest weight, and what is the weight?

Show the answer

Application Environment, Configuration and Security, 25%.

R4What is the passing score and how long is the exam?

Show the answer

66% and 2 hours.

R5How do you reach another host on the exam, and can you SSH from one node to another?

Show the answer

With ssh <node> from base; nested SSH is not allowed, so type exit first.

R6Which command shows the exact name of a Pod spec field for the cluster you are on?

Show the answer

kubectl explain pod.spec (add --recursive for the whole tree).

R7How do you generate a Deployment manifest without creating the Deployment?

Show the answer

Add --dry-run=client -o yaml to kubectl create deployment.

R8Which websites may you open during the exam?

Show the answer

kubernetes.io docs and blog, helm.sh/docs, and the Quick Reference links in the exam; not external search results.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Score 66% to pass; 2 hours; 15 to 20 tasks; state is scored
Weights Environment 25, Design and Build 20, Deployment 20, Networking 20, Observability 15
Start of every task use-context, namespace, exact names
Generate YAML --dry-run=client -o yaml
Find fields kubectl explain ... [--recursive]
Output control -o jsonpath, -o custom-columns, --sort-by, -o wide
Hosts ssh <node>, sudo -i, exit; no nested SSH
Stuck for 6 minutes flag it, move on
